note: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome is well-documented in the literature as an autosomal recessive neuro-ectodermal disorder caused by GTPBP2 variants with intellectual disability, motor delay, microcephaly, and visual impairment.

evidence.text: A literature review of 28 patients with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome associated with GTPBP2 variants demonstrated core phenotypic features including motor development delay in 26/28, sparse hair in 26/28, speech disorder in 24/28, intellectual disability in 23/28, hypotonia in 23/28, skeletal problems in 23/28, and visual impairment in 18/28.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in GTPBP2 cause Jaberi-Elahi syndrome with core clinical features including prenatal-onset microcephaly, tone abnormalities, movement disorders, epilepsy, retinal dysfunction, and ectodermal findings.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Key features of this clinically recognizable condition include prenatal onset microcephaly, tone abnormalities, and movement disorders, epilepsy, dysmorphic features, retinal dysfunction, ectodermal dysplasia, and brain iron accumulation.
